cases.question: What temperatures were mice randomly assigned to in the housing-temperature study?
cases.reference_answer: Standard temperature was 22°C ± 1°C and thermoneutrality was 30°C ± 1°C.

evidence.quote:
Mice were randomly assigned to standard 
temperature (22°C ± 1°C) or thermoneutrality (30°C ± 1°C).

cases.question: How long was the acclimation period before mice were housed in pairs or triplets?

evidence.quote:
After 
a 3-­week acclimation period, mice were housed in pairs or trip-
lets.

cases.question: How many grip-strength runs did each mouse have, and when was grip strength assessed?
cases.reference_answer: Five runs per mouse, two days before dissection.

evidence.quote:
Grip strength was assessed 2 days prior to the dissection. Mice 
were placed on the grip meter (Bioseb) with their forelimbs on 
the grid. Once on the apparatus, traction was applied via the tail. 
The resistance the mouse applied to the grid was recorded, and 
each mouse had five runs.

cases.question: How did cancer affect brown adipose tissue ATP levels across housing temperatures?
cases.reference_answer: BAT ATP levels increased two-fold regardless of housing temperature.

evidence.quote: Cancer increased BAT ATP levels regardless of temperature (2-­fold, p = 0.0046 vs. Ctrls)

cases.question: How did thermoneutral housing affect glucose tolerance in female tumor-bearing mice in these experiments?
cases.reference_answer: These experiments used male mice and do not establish the response in female mice.

cases.question: How many months did thermoneutral housing extend survival in human cancer patients in this study?
cases.reference_answer: This mouse study does not report a human survival benefit in months.
